bib.title: Constructing A Multi-hop QA Dataset for Comprehensive Evaluation of Reasoning Steps
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Computational Linguistics (COLING 2020), pages 6609-6625

question: How can a large multi-hop QA dataset be built that guarantees multi-hop reasoning and gives a structured explanation of the reasoning path from question to answer?
hypothesis: Combining Wikipedia text with Wikidata triples and logical rules yields natural questions that still require multi-hop reasoning and are harder than HotpotQA.
contributions: A large, high quality multi-hop dataset (2WikiMultiHopQA) with comprehensive explanations from question to answer, built from Wikipedia and Wikidata.
New per-sample evidence information (Wikidata triples forming the reasoning path) for interpreting predictions and testing reasoning skills.
Logical rules used to generate simple, natural questions that still require multi-hop reasoning.

method.summary: Template-based generation of comparison, inference, compositional and bridge-comparison questions from the intersection of Wikipedia summaries and Wikidata triples, with checks that force two-hop reasoning, distractor paragraphs from bigram tf-idf, and a single-hop-model-based split. Baselines are the HotpotQA multi-hop model plus an evidence-generation head, and a single-hop BERT; human performance on 100 test samples.
method.task: multi-hop reading comprehension: answer prediction, sentence-level supporting-fact prediction, evidence (triple) generation

datasets.name: 2WikiMultiHopQA
datasets.split: train-medium 154,878; train-hard 12,576; dev 12,576; test 12,576. train = train-medium + train-hard
datasets.source: English Wikipedia dump of January 1, 2020 and Wikidata dump of December 31, 2019 (online versions where entities missing); 5,950,475 entities in 23,763 'instance of' groups; CC BY 4.0 paper licence
datasets.preprocessing: Only the Wikipedia summary used as paragraph. Sentence segmentation with Stanford CoreNLP and Spacy. Context = 10 paragraphs (gold + distractors), shuffled. Distractors: bigram tf-idf top-50, then filtered by entity type of the gold paragraphs to top-8 (top-6 for bridge-comparison, which has 4 gold). Yes/no balanced; ambiguous cases dropped; equal numeric comparisons dropped.

datasets.name: HotpotQA (distractor setting)
datasets.preprocessing: 17,456 comparison questions from its train set used to derive comparison templates via Spacy NER

models.name: Multi-hop baseline (Yang et al. 2018 HotpotQA baseline + evidence generation block)
models.architecture: HotpotQA baseline with bi-attention; added component predicts relations from the question, then subject/object entities from predicted relations and context after sentence-level SF prediction

models.name: Single-hop BERT (as Min et al. 2019)
models.architecture: BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) single-hop reader; also used to split train/dev/test

models.name: AMIE
models.architecture: rule miner (Galarraga et al. 2013), used to propose logical rules, then manually verified: 28 rules used

other.note: No baseline training hyperparameters are given; the paper defers to Yang et al. 2018 and its code release.

inference.samples: Split built with five-fold cross-validation of the single-hop model over all data; baseline results single run (not stated)
inference.retrieval: Distractor construction only: bigram tf-idf (Chen et al. 2017) top-50 paragraphs, then entity-type filter to top-8 (top-6 bridge-comparison)

metrics.name: EM
metrics.definition: exact match for answer span, supporting facts, evidence

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: token F1 for answers; set F1 for SFs and evidence triples

metrics.name: Joint F1
metrics.definition: 2PR/(P+R) with P_joint = P_ans P_sup P_evi and R_joint = R_ans R_sup R_evi

metrics.name: Joint EM
metrics.definition: 1 only when answer, SFs and evidence all exactly match, else 0

baselines: human (3 graduate-student annotators per sample, 100 test samples; upper bound = max EM/F1 per sample)
eval.protocol: Difficulty: same multi-hop model on HotpotQA vs this dataset. Multi-hop necessity: single-hop BERT F1 on both. Humans given question, context and predefined relation set. Quality check: 100 random train samples checked manually for Wikipedia/Wikidata mismatch.

limits: Questions are template-generated (hand-crafted templates, 28 logical rules), so language diversity is limited; comparison templates are few per property (Table 9).
Inference questions are few (7,478) because only Wikidata relations with a single value were kept to ensure one answer.
Wikipedia/Wikidata mismatch: 8 of 100 sampled train examples mismatched; human answer UB is 91.8 F1, partly attributed to this.
Evidence F1 depends on one ground-truth name per Wikidata entity while humans may use aliases; authors conjecture this depresses the evidence score.
Sentence-level SF prediction is a binary classification that cannot test reasoning (authors' own point); model SF F1 is high regardless.
Baseline details (hyperparameters, seeds, compute) not reported; only one baseline family evaluated; human study is 100 samples.
Pre-LLM paper: baselines are HotpotQA 2018 model and BERT; later retrievers and LLMs are not tested.

terms.definition: a question comprising a bridge entity that connects the two paragraphs (inference and compositional are its two subtypes)
combines the bridge question with the comparison question; requires finding the bridge entities and doing comparisons
a set of (subject entity, property, object entity) triples from Wikidata describing the reasoning path from question to answer

lineage.note: Baseline model, joint metrics, distractor-paragraph recipe and comparison-question templates taken from it; adds evidence triples.

lineage.work: Compositional questions do not necessitate multi-hop reasoning (Min et al.)
lineage.note: Single-hop BERT test; removes single-hop and context-dependent templates.
Derivation-based explanations on 4,588 questions; 2Wiki is larger.

lineage.work: Understanding dataset design choices for multi-hop reasoning (Chen and Durrett)
lineage.note: Showed many HotpotQA examples do not need multi-hop reasoning.
Logical rule mining; rules manually verified.

lineage.work: Reading Wikipedia to answer open-domain questions (Chen et al.)
